212418354_02349d4e.text: Medial septal glutamatergic neurons expressing type 2 vesicular glutamate transporters (VGluT2) are likely involved in hippocampal theta generation. 132,135,140 They display a heterogeneous firing pattern, including fast, slow, burs, and clusterfiring (8-14 Hz, half of glutamatergic neurons) properties in slice. 135,137 Glutamatergic neurons also have intrinsic firing properties that may play an important role in pacing the hippocampus in vivo: they can discharge in recurrent clusters of action potentials, interspersed with intrinsically generated subthreshold membrane potential oscillations. 135

212418354_9dc833dc.text: Glutamatergic neurons in the hippocampus display highly heterogeneous electrophysiological properties and firing patterns (Huh et al., 2010)(Senova et al., 2020).

212418354_4007a548.text: This cluster firing pattern occurs at frequencies of 8-14 Hz and is found in approximately half of glutamatergic neurons (Senova et al., 2020). These neurons also show strong action potential accommodation and little or no sag response (Muller et al., 2017).

212418354_157e5fde.text: These intrinsic firing properties may play important roles in pacing hippocampal activity and generating theta oscillations (Senova et al., 2020).
